newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds stable ahead of twin key events.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds stable ahead of twin key events.

text.p: *Australian bonds were reasonably stable in early trading in what could prove to be a key day for future direction with the RBA's Macfarlane due to address a parliamentry committee.
*April labour force data also due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).

Australian bonds were reasonably stable in early trading in what could prove to be a key day for future direction with Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane due to address a federal parliamentary finance committee.

This is the first of Macfarlane's semi-annual testimonies, and the market will scrutinise his initial address and subsequent question and answer session for clues on interest rates policy and the general economic outlook.
The April labour force report is also due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), which is expected to show a strong rebound in employment, but the unemployment rate stuck at 8.7 percent.

"The market's holding up reasonably well given what happened in the U.S. We're confident that Macfarlane is not going to be too negative (for the market), but there again, he's unlikely to be that positive either," one trader said.
U.S. Treasuries fell sharply on Wednesday after a poor performance at the quarterly refunding auctions with a weak response to the 10-year note sale.
Local bond yields spiked sharply yesterday amid heavy liquidation as investors shortened their long positions after the RBA left policy unchanged after Tuesday's monthly board meeting.
